findings.highlight: I'll make you some Tsukemono, so give me dessert.
findings.evidenceJa: 「なぁ、漬物やるからデザートよこせよ」
findings.explanation: Kazusa offers Haruki the pickles from her lunch in exchange for his dessert. She is not offering to make him pickles; the English replaces the immediate bento-swap joke with a nonsensical future act.
findings.japanese: 「なぁ、漬物やるからデザートよこせよ」
findings.todokanai: "I'll make you some Tsukemono, so give me dessert."

findings.highlight: One way or another, we make it closer to our destination, buying nostalgic snacks from the stalls at every station the train stops at.
findings.evidenceJa: 駅の売店で懐かしのアイテムを取り扱ってたりするローカル線の各駅停車は、ゆっくり走ってゆっくり停まり、俺たちの、なんとなく決めた目的地に向かって進む。
findings.explanation: The local all-stops train, whose station kiosks carry nostalgic items, runs slowly and stops slowly toward their loosely chosen destination. The English deletes that languorous train rhythm and invents Haruki and Kazusa buying snacks at every station.
findings.japanese:
駅の売店で懐かしのアイテムを取り扱ってたりする
ローカル線の各駅停車は、ゆっくり走ってゆっくり停まり、
俺たちの、なんとなく決めた目的地に向かって進む。
findings.todokanai: One way or another, we make it closer to our destination, buying nostalgic snacks from the stalls at every station the train stops at.

findings.highlight: Her goal is no longer to eat, or to be spoiled.
findings.evidenceJa:
目的は既に食べることではなく、
甘えることも、その全てではなくて…
findings.explanation: Being coddled is not the whole of Kazusa's purpose; the English says it is no longer her purpose at all — The additional purpose—making Haruki feel shame—is correctly revealed.
findings.japanese:
目的は既に食べることではなく、
甘えることも、その全てではなくて…
findings.todokanai: Her goal is no longer to eat, or to be spoiled.

findings.highlight: the sun itself was denied an appearance behind all the thick layers of snow.
findings.evidenceJa: 白い空、白い木々、白い大地がそびえ…そして、厚い雲に隠された夕陽は、存在そのものを否定されていた。
findings.explanation: The setting sun is hidden behind thick clouds, its very existence denied by the white sky, trees, and earth. The English puts the sun behind thick layers of snow, creating a physically incoherent image and losing the oppressive cloud cover above the white landscape.
findings.japanese:
白い空、白い木々、白い大地がそびえ…
そして、厚い雲に隠された夕陽は、
存在そのものを否定されていた。
findings.todokanai: Between the white sky, the white trees, and the white land… the sun itself was denied an appearance behind all the thick layers of snow.

findings.highlight: we avoided confronting reality with our indiscrete words…
findings.evidenceJa: そんなふうに俺たちは、口では、他愛もない言葉でお茶を濁し…
findings.explanation: Out loud, they muddy the waters with trivial, innocuous words. 'Indiscrete' is both malformed English in context and nearly the opposite register: their spoken conversation is deliberately harmless because their unspeakable true exchange occurs through their eyes.
findings.japanese:
そんなふうに俺たちは、
口では、他愛もない言葉でお茶を濁し…
findings.todokanai: Like that, we avoided confronting reality with our indiscrete words…

findings.highlight: Something that the offenders could not bring themselves to say out loud. Something painful, sorrowful… and full of joy.
findings.evidenceJa: 咎人たちの、とても口には出せない、辛く、痛く…そして悦びにまみれた心の触れ合いを。
findings.explanation: Their true second conversation is a communion or touching of hearts between sinners, too painful and too saturated with pleasure to voice. The English leaves two abstract 'somethings' and drops the governing image of their hearts making contact, which is the point of the spoken-versus-unspoken contrast.
findings.japanese:
咎人たちの、とても口には出せない、
辛く、痛く…そして悦びにまみれた心の触れ合いを。
findings.todokanai: Something that the offenders could not bring themselves to say out loud. Something painful, sorrowful… and full of joy.

findings.highlight: I feel like I'm in someone else's body.
findings.evidenceJa: 「うぁぁ…なんかすごい異物感。次、トイレ行くのが怖い」
findings.explanation: Kazusa feels a pronounced foreign-object sensation inside her after sex and is afraid of her next trip to the toilet. The English says she feels as though she inhabits somebody else's body, an unrelated dissociative claim that breaks the explicit physical joke.
findings.japanese:
「うぁぁ…なんかすごい異物感。
次、トイレ行くのが怖い」
findings.todokanai: "Uwah… I feel like I'm in someone else's body. I'm afraid of going to the toilet next time."

findings.highlight: Kazusa let go of Setsuna's hand, as well as my left hand…
findings.evidenceJa: かずさは五年前に右手を雪菜から離し、そして俺の左手は…
findings.explanation: In the preceding diagram, Setsuna's right hand held Haruki's left while Setsuna's left held Kazusa's right; Haruki and Kazusa's outer hands remained open. Kazusa released her right hand from Setsuna, while Haruki's left has its own unfinished fate. The English falsely says Kazusa also let go of Haruki's left hand, a hand she was never holding.
findings.japanese:
かずさは五年前に右手を雪菜から離し、
そして俺の左手は…
findings.todokanai: Five years ago, Kazusa let go of Setsuna's hand, as well as my left hand…

findings.highlight: she embraces me as I still have my hands on her breasts.
findings.evidenceJa: けれど、未だにその胸にむしゃぶりつく俺を、優しく抱きとめた。
findings.explanation: Kazusa gently holds Haruki while he is still ravenously latched onto her breast. The English changes the ongoing oral action to merely having his hands on her breasts, contradicting the nipple-sucking discussion and the detailed continuation five lines later.
findings.japanese:
けれど、未だにその胸にむしゃぶりつく俺を、
優しく抱きとめた。
findings.todokanai: But still, she embraces me as I still have my hands on her breasts.

findings.highlight: it's difficult to tell if it actually is daytime.
findings.evidenceJa: 空は暗く、地面は明るく、その景色はまるで色を変えず、だから、今が昼間ということしかわからないくらい時間の感覚が奪われる。
findings.explanation: The unchanging dark sky and bright ground rob them of time to such a degree that all they can tell is that it is daytime. The English says even daytime itself is difficult to determine, reversing the one temporal fact the Japanese explicitly leaves available.
findings.japanese:
空は暗く、地面は明るく、その景色はまるで色を変えず、
だから、今が昼間ということしかわからないくらい
時間の感覚が奪われる。
findings.todokanai: The sky is dark, the ground is bright, and nothing changes with time. Because of that, it's difficult to tell if it actually is daytime. I'm completely robbed of my perception of time.

findings.highlight: hold on, I was supposed to stop thinking about that.
findings.evidenceJa: それはまるで、子供に乳を与える母親の…って、俺にはそんなイメージ湧かないんだった。
findings.explanation: The nursing-mother image fails to arise for Haruki because, as the immediately preceding lines establish, his memories of his own mother vanished or were forcibly erased. The English invents a conscious rule that he was 'supposed to stop thinking' about mothers, replacing traumatic absence with voluntary restraint; line 460 repeats the invented promise.
findings.japanese:
それはまるで、子供に乳を与える母親の…
って、俺にはそんなイメージ湧かないんだった。
findings.todokanai: Almost like a mother forcing her child to drink her milk… hold on, I was supposed to stop thinking about that.

findings.highlight: aah, not there…
findings.evidenceJa: 「ぅ、んっ…あ、あぁ…春希ぃ。あ、そこ…ふぅぅんっ、ん、んぅぅ…」
findings.explanation: Kazusa cries 'there' as Haruki stimulates the right spot. The English adds 'not,' turning an affirmative response of pleasure into a request that he stop or move elsewhere.
findings.japanese:
「ぅ、んっ…あ、あぁ…春希ぃ。
あ、そこ…ふぅぅんっ、ん、んぅぅ…」
findings.todokanai: "Uah, ahmm… aah, Haruki… aah, not there… aaah!"

findings.highlight: And this isn't about Kazusa; it's about me too…
findings.evidenceJa: かずさじゃなくて、俺の方が…
findings.explanation: The anxiety that cannot be stopped belongs not to Kazusa but to Haruki. Adding 'too' makes the fear shared and weakens the correction: all his efforts to calm and distract Kazusa are really attempts to control his own panic.
findings.japanese: かずさじゃなくて、俺の方が…
findings.todokanai: And this isn't about Kazusa; it's about me too…

findings.highlight: by burying myself deeper into Kazusa's chest.
findings.evidenceJa: だから俺は、胸の奥から湧き出てくるそんな不安を押し潰すために、かずさで、胸の奥をいっぱいにする。
findings.explanation: To crush the anxiety welling from deep in his heart, Haruki fills the depths of that heart with Kazusa. The English literalizes 胸 twice and makes him physically bury himself in her chest, erasing the psychological substitution by which he tries to crowd out fear.
findings.japanese:
だから俺は、胸の奥から湧き出てくる
そんな不安を押し潰すために、
かずさで、胸の奥をいっぱいにする。
findings.todokanai: That's why I try to suppress the anxiety gushing from my chest by burying myself deeper into Kazusa's chest.

findings.highlight: her extreme introversion will become even more prominent when we're alone together.
findings.evidenceJa: …おかげで二人きりになった後の内向的な激しさが、ますます際立っていくことになる訳だけど。
findings.explanation: The joke contrasts Kazusa's public shyness with the fierce intensity she directs inward or privately once the two are alone. The English says her introversion itself becomes more prominent in private, missing the sexual-personality reversal and producing a claim that does not fit her uninhibited behavior with Haruki.
findings.japanese:
…おかげで二人きりになった後の内向的な激しさが、
ますます際立っていくことになる訳だけど。
findings.todokanai: …Thanks to that, her extreme introversion will become even more prominent when we're alone together.

findings.highlight: Maybe I was just a bit dizzy, because right now her skin is as pink as a cherry blossom.
findings.evidenceJa: 「あらあらごめんなさい見立て違いでした。ちょっとのぼせたみたいですねぇ。いつの間にか桜の花みたいになっちゃいました」
findings.explanation: The hostess revises her snow-white comparison because Kazusa now seems flushed or overheated and has turned cherry-blossom pink from embarrassment. The English makes the hostess herself dizzy, disconnecting the temperature joke from Kazusa's visible blush.
findings.japanese:
「あらあらごめんなさい見立て違いでした。
ちょっとのぼせたみたいですねぇ。
いつの間にか桜の花みたいになっちゃいました」
findings.todokanai: "Oh, I'm so sorry, I must've seen wrong. Maybe I was just a bit dizzy, because right now her skin is as pink as a cherry blossom."

findings.highlight: The hostess fell for my desperate attempt at a diversion
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の必死のすり替えに、仲居さんは乗ってくれてたけど、その視線はずっとかずさの顔から離れなかった。
findings.explanation: The hostess goes along with Haruki's desperate substitution story, but never takes her eyes off Kazusa; Haruki therefore knows she recognized her. 'Fell for' says the deception succeeded, contradicting both the Japanese implication of indulgent complicity and Haruki's immediate conclusion that she definitely knows.
findings.japanese:
俺の必死のすり替えに、
仲居さんは乗ってくれてたけど、
その視線はずっとかずさの顔から離れなかった。
findings.todokanai: The hostess fell for my desperate attempt at a diversion, but she never looked away from Kazusa's face.

findings.highlight: We exchange our vows, and hold our wedding ceremony.
findings.evidenceJa:
互いの誓いの言葉にのっとり、
夫婦の儀式を、執り行う。
findings.explanation: 夫婦の儀式 is the marital or conjugal rite, strongly implying consummating sex under their vows; 'wedding ceremony' makes it only nuptial pageantry — The vows, naked embrace, and ensuing ellipsis leave the consummation recoverable.
findings.japanese:
互いの誓いの言葉にのっとり、
夫婦の儀式を、執り行う。
findings.todokanai: We exchange our vows, and hold our wedding ceremony.

findings.highlight: Without any regard to the fact that I would have prevented her from going outside.
findings.evidenceJa: しかも外に出ることを、俺に止められていたにもかかわらず。
findings.explanation: Kazusa goes out despite Haruki having forbidden or stopped her from leaving the inn. The English changes that prior restriction into a hypothetical claim that he would have stopped her, weakening why her unexplained absence appears so alarming.
findings.japanese:
しかも外に出ることを、
俺に止められていたにもかかわらず。
findings.todokanai: Without any regard to the fact that I would have prevented her from going outside.

findings.highlight: So she wouldn't be able to see that I'm on the brink of tears.
findings.evidenceJa: …思わずこぼれてしまった涙を見られないために。
findings.explanation: Haruki evades Kazusa so she will not see the tears that have already spilled despite him. The English pulls him back to merely being on the brink, reducing the concrete emotional release that explains his flustered anger and refusal to face her.
findings.japanese: …思わずこぼれてしまった涙を見られないために。
findings.todokanai: …So she wouldn't be able to see that I'm on the brink of tears.
